> 「佛得阿耨多罗三藐三菩提，为无所得耶？」佛言：「如是，如是。须菩提！我于阿耨多罗三藐三菩提，乃至无有少法可得，是名阿耨多罗三藐三菩提。」

Section twenty-two is four lines long. It is also where the sutra settles its accounts.

须菩提 asks: so the Buddha's awakening — was it a non-attainment? Yes, yes, says the Buddha. Not even the smallest dharma was obtained. That is what is called perfect awakening.

## 如是，如是 is a double seal

The doubled affirmation is unusual. The book reads it as sealing two things: the question as asked, and what the question left unsaid.

What the question leaves unsaid is the residue — the small hope that "non-attainment" might itself be something. The second 如是 closes that.

## 乃至无有少法可得

乃至: extending even to. 少法: the least dharma, a hair, a trace, a shred.

So: not merely no great attainment, but no minimum remainder. The negation is run all the way down until there is nothing left to hold, including a subtle one.

The book's observation about what this actually negates: the mind that wanted to get something. Practice still cuts confusion, and confusion being cut is a real event. What does not exist is someone who has obtained the cutting.

## The gap this section is built to close

By this point in the sutra, a reader has been trained. Marks are cancelled; bodies are denied as evidence; merit is emptied; the teaching itself is declared unspoken. Such a reader is now in danger of a specific error — the error of having learned the lesson.

Having learned it, one holds the conclusion: *ultimately, nothing is attained.* And that conclusion is exactly a 少法: a small dharma, gripped.

This is what the twenty-second section is for. It is not a repetition of the earlier negations; it is their audit. Every previous cancellation left an implicit remainder — "at least the cancellation is real". Here the remainder is cancelled.

## 是名 returns immediately

The sentence does not end in nihilism. It ends with naming: 是名阿耨多罗三藐三菩提.

Non-attainment is not the truth of the matter, announced from a height. It is the name the tradition uses for awakening. Use it, and do not mistake the name for the thing — the same instruction the sutra gave about its own title nine sections ago.

## The test

Find the conclusion you are most confident about. Preferably a hard-won one — something you worked out, suffered for, and now know.

Ask the section's question of it: is this one of the dharmas you have obtained?

If it is, then it is the 少法 — the least dharma — and the sutra has just said that not even that was obtained. Which does not make your conclusion false. It makes it something you are holding.
